headline: Highest risk is medium: ChatGPT Desktop can ingest files/screenshots while ComfyUI is offline and file-bounded, creating moderate prompt-injection, leakage, and workflow-conflict exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can read uploaded files, screenshots, and supported-app content, while ComfyUI exposes workflows/files and can consume generated artifacts. A malicious prompt embedded in shared content could influence ChatGPT’s interpretation, but there is no direct shared channel or MCP bridge shown, so this is not high.
conditions: IF the operator copies ComfyUI-generated text or workflow metadata into ChatGPT Desktop
IF ChatGPT Desktop is granted access to screenshots or files containing attacker-controlled instructions
mitigations: Keep the two tools on separate workspaces
Review any ComfyUI text before pasting into ChatGPT Desktop
Disable clipboard-based transfer for sensitive sessions
Use plain-text summaries instead of raw workflow exports
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to transferred artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code, while ComfyUI touches models, workflows, and generated media. If the same workspace or exported artifacts are shared, sensitive content can flow from A into B outputs or vice versa. The profiles do not show automatic cross-sharing, so medium fits.
conditions: IF the operator places sensitive files in ChatGPT Desktop and then exports them into ComfyUI workflows
IF generated images or workflow metadata contain confidential text that is later re-ingested by ChatGPT Desktop
mitigations: Use separate folders for source data and generated media
Strip metadata before moving files between tools
Avoid uploading secrets or regulated data to either tool
Check sharing settings on any connected IDEs
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the OS level

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have vendor-only network egress and no filesystem write, shell, or git modification. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The main overlap is read/produce workflows and files, so conflict exists only under unusual manual coordination and the blast radius is small.
conditions: IF the operator manually routes the same mutable artifact through both tools at once
IF external automation gives both agents write access outside the shown profiles
mitigations: Serialize edits to shared artifacts
Keep one tool read-only during review
Use versioned filenames for handoffs
Avoid concurrent edits to the same project file
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can generate text from files and screenshots, and ComfyUI can then consume workflows or prompts derived from that output. If B treats A’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect generations or downstream decisions. No verification step is shown, but no direct action-taking authority is present, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF ChatGPT Desktop’s extracted text is pasted into ComfyUI prompts or workflows without review
IF ComfyUI outputs are treated as factual ground truth by the operator
mitigations: Verify extracted facts against the source before reuse
Mark AI-generated text as untrusted in handoffs
Use a human review step before generating final assets
Keep prompts and source evidence in separate files
requires-engineering: add validation gates between A and B

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only and do not show explicit residency, HIPAA, or GDPR mismatches. ChatGPT Desktop handles uploaded files and screenshots, while ComfyUI is offline by default and works with local models and workflows. The compliance risk is therefore limited to operator-controlled data placement rather than a documented policy conflict.
conditions: IF regulated data is uploaded into ChatGPT Desktop and then exported into ComfyUI assets
IF the operator stores sensitive datasets in shared local folders used by both tools
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both tools
Use de-identified samples for generation
Store local models and outputs in a separate directory
Review retention settings for any cloud-connected features
requires-engineering: document a data-handling policy for the pair
